unit.why: R. Yitzhak of Vorka tells how, troubled by his wife's harsh treatment of himself and his servants, he travelled to R. David of Lelov and later understood his cryptic answer through a teaching of the Besht. The story is embedded in a compilation of homiletic quotations on the same theme.
unit.boundary_note: the story is followed in the same division by non-narrative quotations from אור צדיקים, אוצר החיים and משמרת איתמר

stories.start_quote: סיפר מורי בוצ״ק הרב מהר״י מווארקא
stories.summary_en: R. Yitzhak of Vorka told the great men sitting before him that in his youth he suffered from his wife and could not bear how she treated his servants; he went to ask R. David of Lelov, who answered 'what do you tell me, tell yourself', and only later, through a teaching of the Besht on thought, speech and action, did he understand that everything depends on the master of the house himself.

tags.why: The tsaddik narrates his own experience to an assembly of great men.
